critical_code_review_comments: Band thresholds + debounce live as magic numbers inside /score (0.70/0.40/0.20 and streak>=2). Consider extracting band edges + debounce_n to module-level constants (or per-device cfg) so future tuning doesn't risk silent drift between code and tests.

Additive trust uses weighted MEAN over AVAILABLE factors -- if only behaviour is sent (no pin/known_device/lat/lng/screen), a single bad typing reading can drop trust below 0.20 and still escalate to L2/L3. This matches the original behaviour-only tests but means an old client that doesn't send pin_ok/known_device can produce more aggressive escalation than a new client. Document the expectation that production clients should always send pin_ok (true/false) so the 15% pin floor stabilises the score.

/recovery/call-trigger uses suffix match: norm.replace(' ','').endswith(a.replace(' ','')[-7:]). This treats '+15551234567' and '+19995551234567' as trusted if the last 7 digits collide -- low probability but real. Consider an exact normalised E.164 match (or a hash) instead of a 7-digit suffix.

ScoreRequest.known_device is Optional[float] but semantically it's 0/1 or a 0-1 confidence; document the contract and consider clamping at the pydantic layer (Field(ge=0, le=1)) rather than inside _score, so bad client input is rejected at the API edge.

Setup clamps call_trigger_count to 1-10 and window to 30-1800s but silently coerces out-of-range values -- a client asking for count=0 quietly gets 1. Either echo the effective value back in the response or 400 on out-of-range so misconfiguration is visible.

OWNER_TRUST_THRESHOLD (0.70) is referenced both in /score body (is_owner = trust >= 0.70) and in the band branch (`if trust >= 0.70`); the second uses a literal not the constant. Reuse OWNER_TRUST_THRESHOLD to keep band-edge and is_owner in lockstep.
